tools.name: get_booking_page
tools.description: Look up a public Yoya booking page. Pass its slug (the part after yoya.ai/) or the whole link — either works. Returns the host name, meeting title/description, meeting length, the meeting options offered (google_meet / zoom / in_person), and any fields the guest must provide to book. Returns null if

tools.name: list_available_times
tools.description: Return the open time slots for a booking page, identified by its slug or its full link. Each slot has an opaque `id` and a human-readable `time` label in the host's timezone. Pass a slot `id` to book_meeting — never invent a time; only these ids are bookable.

tools.name: book_meeting
tools.description: Book a meeting on a host's page. Use a slot `id` from list_available_times (a time not in that list will be rejected). `email` is required — the confirmation and calendar invite go there. tools.name: get_booking
tools.description: Look up a booking by its manage token (the code in a yoya.ai/b/<token> link) to see its status and time.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "book" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: book_meeting · Private data: get_booking · Public sink: book_meeting.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: book_meeting · Private data: get_booking · Public sink: book_meeting

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
